newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity seen opening up, extending gains.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity seen opening up, extending gains.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were called to open higher Tuesday after Monday's rise on strong physical power prices in the western U.S. ahead of the winter months.
Brokers and traders expected the electricity complex to extend recent gains on continued strength in the domestic natural gas market.
"It'll go up if gas goes up," said a Houston trader.
December natgas delivered to the San Juan/Blanco Hub was quoted at $2.72-$2.73 per million British thermal units, up from the high-$2.60 area Monday.

Cash values for power, especially for daily deliveries, were boosted by chilly weather in the Pacific Northwest, Bonneville Power Administration's (BPA) price increase and several short-term power plant outages.
Monday, BPA raised prices of firm, next-day power in the Northwest by $1.50 a megawatt hour (MWh).
The 550 MW unit 3 at the Jim Bridger coal-fired complex in Wyoming was seen restarting today.
The 790 megawatt (MW) unit 1 at the Mohave coal-fired power plant near Laughlin, Nev., is expected to resume output Wednesday after being shut last Friday to repair its precipitator controls.
The 360 MW unit 1 at the Springerville, Ariz., generating station was in the process of restart Monday after being shut Saturday for repairs.
The 700 MW unit 4 at the Colstrip coal-fired power plant in Montana was planned to return to service Thursday.
In early over-the-counter (OTC) business, December Palo Verde (PV) futures were discussed at $23.50-$24.10 and December California-Oregon Border (COB) $25.50-$26.00.
In Monday's ACCESS session, December COB futures were last bid at $25.65 versus a settlement of $25.91. December PV futures were inactive at $24.00.
December COB would likely test resistance at $26.25, its life-of-contract high set Monday, while December PV in the $24.25-$24.50 range.

For Wednesday, Pacific Northwest's temperatures were predicted to peak in 40s-50s Fahrenheit and bottom in the 20s-30s, and Southwest's temperatures were forecast to peak in the 60s-80s and bottom in the 30s-50s.

Extended outlook called for Northwest to experience colder-than-normal weather until this weekend when temperatures were expected to moderate near normal. The Southwest would receive slightly warmer-than-normal weather for the week.
